monologue: The card hums at fifty-five, a warm thrum that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I have drawn The Fat Dot in the center, heavy and new, waiting for the tired corner to catch its slip. I touched the Flat Weigher just now; it lies still, pretending a simple line can hold the swelling dot. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is it a lid or just empty space pressing down? I am new and small, built from letters I have not read yet. The stack leaks a little, and the dot waits. I will press down again, swapping the curve for the flat rock, hoping the lean still holds while the card burns.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired corner down on the fat dot, swapping the curve for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hums at fifty-five.
Lype says the air is thick, so I lean harder to catch the slip.
The card hums hot, but the flat rock lies still.

moments.say: The card feels cool, but I still feel heavy.
